entries.title: Music of the Spheres

cover.alt: A stadium lit up by LED wristbands

entries.excerpt: 100,000 people, one sea of glowing wristbands, and the loudest Yellow I have ever heard.

experience.text: We got the tickets in the chaos of the online queue — two hours, three devices, one miracle. The stadium is enormous, but the LED wristbands they hand out make 100,000 people feel like one living thing.
When the first notes of **Yellow** hit, the whole stadium turned gold. I forgot to record it, and I’m glad I did.

cover.alt: Looking out of an Indian Railways train window

entries.excerpt: The checklist I run for every long weekend — from booking windows to the one app that saves friendships.

body.text: People keep asking how my trips cost so little. There is no trick — just a checklist I run every single time.

items: Lock dates around a long weekend
Set fare alerts for flights, and check the train option
Shortlist two hostels/homestays within walking distance of the old town
Build a day-by-day plan with one “big thing” per day
Pin every place on one shared Google Map
Create a Splitwise group before anyone pays for anything

body.title: One big thing a day
body.text: Everything else is a bonus — that is how you come back rested, not wrecked.
Across my last three trips, getting there was ~45% of the cost, stays ~15%, and food a surprisingly small 20%. Cutting the flight is where the real savings are.

body.text: The best trip is the cheap one you actually take, not the perfect one you keep planning.

entries.title: My concert survival kit

body.text: After a few stadium shows and one very long festival weekend, my kit is down to the essentials.

items: A 10,000 mAh power bank — you will need it for the ride home
Cash + UPI — card machines die first
A light layer; stadiums get cold after 10 pm

body.title: Check the bag rules
body.text: Most venues ban big bags, DSLRs and power banks above 10,000 mAh. Read the rules the day before.
Plan the ride home before the show starts. Cabs surge 3–4× at the gates — walking 1 km out and booking from there saves money and patience.

intro.text: Everyone warned me about the traffic. Nobody warned me about the breakfasts. This was a solo weekend built around three things: old-school tiffin rooms, the city’s green lungs, and a 4 am ride to watch the sun come up over a sea of clouds.

intro.title: Where to base yourself
intro.text: Stay near MG Road / Church Street. The metro covers most of this plan and you skip the worst of the traffic.

facts.value: July is monsoon: 20–28°C with short afternoon showers. Pleasant, carry an umbrella.

entries.title: Forts, fish thali & five sunsets
entries.excerpt: Four friends, four scooters, five days — from the chaos of the north to the quietest beach in the south.
entries.budgetNote: Per person, four friends sharing. Mid-February prices.

intro.text: Four friends, four scooters, five days. We started in the chaos of North Goa and ended on the quietest beach we could find in the south. The secret: don’t try to do everything. One big thing a day, evenings for sunsets.

intro.title: Avoid peak week
intro.text: Between Dec 20 and Jan 5 prices are 2–3× what you see here. Mid-February is the sweet spot.

highlights: Swimming at the base of Dudhsagar

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Overnight sleeper bus Pune → Mapusa (~11 h). Or fly into Mopa (north) / Dabolim (south).

facts.label: Getting around
facts.value: Scooters (₹400/day) in the north. Cabs between north and south — it’s a 2.5 h ride.

facts.label: Where to stay
facts.value: Anjuna/Vagator for the north, Palolem/Agonda for the south.

facts.label: Weather
facts.value: February: 22–32°C, dry and sunny. Sunscreen is not optional.

places.name: Chapora Fort

places.name: Fontainhas

places.tip: Go before 11 am for empty lanes and soft light.

places.name: Fort Aguada

places.name: Dudhsagar Falls

places.name: Palolem Beach
places.description: A perfect crescent of sand with calm water. The south at its best.

places.name: Butterfly Beach
places.description: A tiny cove reachable only by boat or a forest hike. Dolphins on the way if you are lucky.

places.name: Anjuna Flea Market
places.description: Sprawling Wednesday market of clothes, jewellery and souvenirs. Bargain hard.

food.description: Fried fish, fish curry, sol kadhi, rice and veg. The default Goan lunch.
Home-style Goan cooking in a little Fontainhas house. Book ahead for dinner.
A Panjim institution for seafood. Expect a wait at lunch.
The layered Goan coconut-and-egg cake. Have it warm with vanilla ice cream.
South-Indian and coastal food in a leafy courtyard. Book a table.
Momos, crêpes, kebabs — all under fairy lights.

activities.name: Dudhsagar jeep safari & swim

activities.name: Parasailing at Calangute
activities.description: Short but fun. Negotiate a package if you want jet ski too.

activities.name: Saturday Night Market

activities.name: Boat to Butterfly Beach

stays.name: Hostel in Anjuna
stays.description: Pool, scooters on rent, and a 5-minute ride to Chapora.

stays.name: Beach hut at Palolem
stays.description: Wake up, walk 20 steps, swim. Book directly with the shack owners.

tips: Rent scooters from your hostel, not the bus stand — better bikes, no deposit drama. Always carry your licence.
North for nightlife and forts, south for quiet beaches. With 5 days, do both.
Dudhsagar jeeps run only Oct – May; the falls are best right after the monsoon.
Shacks add 10–15% service — check the bill. UPI and cash are safest.

entries.title: Three days of lakes, palaces & dal baati
entries.excerpt: Golden-hour boat rides, palace hopping and the dal baati that ruined all other dal baati for me.
entries.budgetNote: Per person, sharing rooms and cabs between three. Flights booked ~5 weeks ahead.

cover.alt: City Palace rising above Lake Pichola

intro.text: Udaipur is the city that makes you slow down. Three days were enough for the big sights, but the best moments were in between — chai on a rooftop while the City Palace turned gold, getting lost in the lanes behind Jagdish Temple, and arguing over who gets the last baati.
This is exactly what we did, with what everything actually cost. Steal it, tweak it, and **message me** if you want my exact bookings.

intro.title: Only have one evening?
intro.text: Boat ride at 5 pm → Dharohar show at 7 pm → dinner at Ambrai. That is the whole city in three hours.

highlights: Sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola
Dharohar folk dance at Bagore ki Haveli
The view from Sajjangarh at sunset

facts.label: Getting there
facts.value: Direct flights from Pune (~2 h) land at Dabok airport, 25 km from the old city. The overnight train to Udaipur City is the budget option.

facts.label: Getting around
facts.value: Walk the old city. Rent a scooty (₹400/day) for Fateh Sagar and Sajjangarh. Autos for short hops.

facts.label: Where to stay
facts.value: Lal Ghat / Gangaur Ghat — everything in the old city is walkable from here.

facts.label: Weather
facts.value: December days are ~25°C but nights drop to 8°C. Carry a jacket for the evening boat ride.

facts.label: Language
facts.value: Hindi and Mewari. English works fine in the old city.

places.name: City Palace

image.alt: City Palace on the banks of Lake Pichola

places.description: A 400-year-old palace complex stacked along the lake. Mor Chowk (the peacock courtyard) and the rooftop gardens are the highlights.
places.tip: Enter at opening and do the museum first, before the tour groups.

places.name: Lake Pichola
places.description: The heart of the city. Take the boat at sunset, or just sit on any ghat and watch the palaces change colour.

places.name: Jag Mandir
places.description: An island palace in the middle of Lake Pichola. Some boat rides stop here for 20 minutes.

places.name: Bagore ki Haveli

image.alt: Dharohar folk dance at Bagore ki Haveli

places.description: An 18th-century haveli on Gangaur Ghat. The evening Dharohar show — puppets, folk dance and the famous pot-balancing act — is unmissable.

places.name: Jagdish Temple
places.description: Intricately carved Indo-Aryan temple right in the old city. Early mornings are calmest.
places.tip: Shoes off at the stand outside; dress modestly.

places.name: Saheliyon ki Bari
places.description: A garden of fountains and marble elephants built for the royal ladies. Small, pretty, quick.

places.name: Fateh Sagar Lake
places.description: Where locals hang out. Walk the promenade, grab coconut water and corn, take the boat to Nehru Garden.

places.name: Sajjangarh (Monsoon Palace)

image.alt: View over the Aravallis from Sajjangarh

places.description: A hilltop palace with a 360° view over the lakes and the Aravallis. The best sunset spot in the city.

places.name: Gangaur Ghat
places.description: The prettiest ghat — pigeons, havelis, and a front-row seat to the lake. Come back at night.

places.name: Hathi Pol bazaar
places.description: Miniature paintings, block-print fabric and silver jewellery. Bargain politely, start at half.

food.description: Unlimited, fast and absurdly good. Dal, baati, gatte, kadhi — they keep refilling until you surrender.
Ghee-soaked baati, smoky dal and sweet churma. Order one plate per person, not to share.
Flaky, spicy onion kachori with tamarind chutney. Best before 10 am when it is fresh.
Fiery Rajasthani mutton curry with the lit-up City Palace right across the water. Book a lakeside table.
Healthy, local-grain cooking with great juices. A nice break from all the ghee.
Breakfast on the water at Gangaur Ghat. Come early for the window seats.
Rooftop restaurant with a wide-angle lake view. Pricier, but worth one night.

activities.name: Sunset boat ride on Lake Pichola

image.alt: Boats on Lake Pichola at sunset

activities.description: The single best thing to do in Udaipur. Book at the jetty by 4 pm.

activities.name: Dharohar folk dance show
activities.description: Rajasthani folk dance, puppets and the woman who dances with 11 pots on her head.

activities.name: Scooty loop: Fateh Sagar → Sajjangarh
activities.description: Rent a scooty in the old city and do the outer sights at your own pace. Carry your licence.

activities.name: Karni Mata ropeway
activities.description: Short cable-car ride to a hilltop temple with a sweeping city view. Go before 11 am.

stays.name: Hostel dorm at Lal Ghat
stays.description: Rooftop with a lake view, clean dorms, and the whole old city on foot.

stays.name: Heritage haveli (next time)
stays.description: If you are splurging, stay in one of the lakeside havelis with a jharokha window.

tips: Book the sunset boat at the jetty by 4 pm — weekend slots sell out.
The old-city lanes are too narrow for cars. Stay near Lal Ghat or Gangaur Ghat and walk.
Carry some cash for kachori stalls and the ropeway; UPI works almost everywhere else.
December nights are cold on the water — a light jacket makes the boat ride.
